title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
why_read: A rigorous new benchmark exposing how poorly even strong LLMs translate natural language security requests into correct Kali Linux command-line syntax, relevant to anyone building AI security tooling.
analysis: KaliBench is a large benchmark, over 8,500 query-command pairs across 1,642 cybersecurity tools, that tests whether language models can correctly turn a plain-English request into an exact, executable command-line invocation for tools used in penetration testing and other security phases. The key finding is that even strong open-weight models top out around 42% exact-command accuracy without hints, showing that command-line precision is a much harder and more brittle problem than general security knowledge quizzes suggest. They also show that targeted fine-tuning and reinforcement learning using this benchmark's verifiable reward signal can bring a small 8B model up to the performance of a much larger 685B model. This is useful empirical grounding for anyone evaluating AI-driven security automation tools rather than hype.
